1.why: Reset validation requires token === session.resetToken for the caller’s session after that session requested reset for the mock account.

2.why: The reset token is stored only on the requesting session; another session has no matching resetToken so the same code does not work for others.

3.why: password-update only mutates the current session and never deletes or invalidates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS certs and HTTP is rejected, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and session fields are stored in plaintext in memory with no encryption of reset codes or user data.

6.why: No real email is sent; the API uses a generic account-existence message and does not embed profile data in a message body.

7.why: Email/token/password inputs are type-checked and validated; the UI builds nodes with textContent only, avoiding HTML injection.

8.why: There are no user-controlled redirect targets; navigation is internal screen state and fetch paths are fixed.

9.why: Delivery is simulated locally with no email template that interpolates user-supplied HTML or scripts.

10.why: Error JSON is generic and stack traces are swallowed, but mock reset/MFA tokens are returned in API JSON and written into the on-page logs UI.

11.why: Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes in session state, but MFA_CODE is hardcoded in source as "482913".

12.why: The fixed demo MFA_CODE and MOCK_ACCOUNT_EMAIL act as built-in default credentials for completing recovery.

13.why: rateAllowed limits reset-request (3/15m), reset-validate (5/15m), and mfa-verify (5/15m) attempts per session.

14.why: reset-request always returns the same generic message and a mockDeliveryToken whether or not the email is the known mock account.

15.why: reset tokens are 32-byte crypto random base64url values stored on the issuing session and compared strictly server-side.
